label: thm:full-couette-final
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The threshold $\varepsilon\lesssim\nu$ has the same exponent as
the results of Wei--Zhang \cite{WeiZhang2021} on
$\mathbb T\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb T$ and Chen--Wei--Zhang
\cite{ChenWeiZhang2024} in a finite channel with no-slip
boundary conditions.
This scale is also consistent with the sharp linear lift-up
mechanism on $\mathbb T\times\mathbb R^2$.
Indeed, the linearized zero mode satisfies
\[
 u^{1}_{0}(t)
 =\mathrm e^{\nu t\Delta_\perp}
 \bigl(u^1_{0,\mathrm{in}}-t u^2_{0,\mathrm{in}}\bigr).
\]
For suitable roll data supported in a fixed transverse
frequency annulus, an initial perturbation of size $\varepsilon$
produces a streak of size $\varepsilon/\nu$ at times
$t\sim\nu^{-1}$.
Thus $\varepsilon\lesssim\nu$ is the natural scale for remaining
in a fixed small neighborhood of Couette flow.
The present theorem attains this scale despite the absence of
a spanwise spectral gap, with the transverse low frequencies
controlled by the additional endpoint Besov assumption.
head: environment

label: rem:full-roll-sufficiency-final
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:full-roll-sufficiency-final}
The criticality in \eqref{eq:intro-liftup-characterization} concerns
linear lift-up of $u^2_{0}$. The condition on $u^3_{0}$ is used to
propagate the full nonlinear roll and its quadratic stresses. Thus
\eqref{eq:main-smallness-final} is a sufficient nonlinear stability
criterion.
head: environment

label: rem:stability-scale-final
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:stability-scale-final}
At $\varepsilon=c_*\nu$, lift-up permits a streak of size
$\varepsilon/\nu=O(c_*)$, while the roll and the low-order nonzero-mode
bounds remain $O(\varepsilon)$. The two scales in
\eqref{eq:full-energy-final} reflect this distinction. The theorem
therefore gives uniform smallness relative to the fixed Couette flow,
with enhanced dissipation of the streamwise-dependent part and
algebraic decay of the roll.
head: environment

label: thm:global-decay-final
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: rem:no-physical-H1-decay-revised
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:no-physical-H1-decay-revised}
Estimate \eqref{eq:global-inviscid-damping} is a time-integrated form
of inviscid damping: its constant is independent of viscosity, and no
positive power of $\nu$ is placed before the norm. It is stronger than
the $L^2_t$ bound obtained by integrating enhanced dissipation alone,
which loses $\nu^{-1/6}$. A pointwise $t^{-2}$ nonlinear damping rate
is not asserted here. The exponential bound with $O(\varepsilon)$
amplitude in \eqref{eq:full-ED-final} is stated in physical $L^2$;
physical wall-normal derivatives also contain shear-induced growth.
head: environment

label: cor:homogeneous-Hminus2
title: Corollary
head: environment

label: rem:homogeneous-versus-inhomogeneous
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:homogeneous-versus-inhomogeneous}
The space in \Cref{cor:homogeneous-Hminus2} is homogeneous.
The inhomogeneous $H^{-2}$ norm is already controlled by $L^2$ and
adds no condition at the transverse origin. Although
$\dot H^{-2}=\dot B^{-2}_{2,2}$ embeds into
$\dot B^{-2}_{2,\infty}$, it does not contain general projected
divergences of $L^1$ tensors; an explicit example is given after
\Cref{prop:linear-criticality}. Consequently, the stronger Sobolev
condition is imposed only on the initial data, and propagation is
carried out in the endpoint Besov space.
head: environment

label: cor:weighted-initial-data
title: Corollary
head: environment

label: rem:weighted-roll-condition
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:weighted-roll-condition}
The weights in \Cref{cor:weighted-initial-data} are required only for
the initial roll, not for the full three-dimensional perturbation.
Incompressibility and the first moment imply zero transverse mean
and $|\widehat u^\perp_{0,\rm in}(\xi_\perp)|\lesssim|\xi_\perp|$,
which is sufficient for the Besov condition. Such first-order
vanishing need not give a finite $\dot H^{-2}$ norm. The weighted
criterion therefore covers data not included in
\Cref{cor:homogeneous-Hminus2}; no propagation of the spatial moment
is needed.
head: environment

label: rem:streak-endpoint-decay
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:streak-endpoint-decay}
Uniform streak control should be distinguished from streak decay.
Even for the linearized equations, the endpoint condition does not
force $t\mathrm e^{\nu t\Delta_{\!\perp}}u^2_{0,\rm in}$ to tend to zero in $L^2$.
For example, let $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ be real, even, and equal to one
near the origin and set
$\widehat u^\perp_{0,\rm in}(\eta,\ell)
=i(-\ell,\eta)\chi(\eta,\ell)$.
This is a divergence-free Schwartz roll, but a change of variables
$\xi_\perp=(\nu t)^{-1/2}\zeta$ shows that
$\|t\mathrm e^{\nu t\Delta_{\!\perp}}u^2_{0,\rm in}\|_{L^2}$ tends to a positive
multiple of $\nu^{-1}$. This explains why
\eqref{eq:full-zero-final} states boundedness rather than a decay
rate for the streak.

Elapsed time after physical time one is denoted by $t$. The shear and the algebraic unknown $q$ are reconstructed from the translated velocity. The correctors are solved anew with

(\Delta u^3_{\neq}-2\partial_xq^{(3)})(0)=\Delta u^3_{\neq}(0).

The low-order initial scale is $\varepsilon$, whereas the high-order scale is $\varepsilon/\nu$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The global energy bounds \eqref{eq:full-energy-final} have already
been obtained. In the following estimates, $s$ denotes elapsed time
after the restart, so physical time is $t=1+s$. All $s$-norms are
taken over $[0,\infty)$, and $E_4(\infty):=\sup_{T>0}E_4(T)$.

For the nonzero modes, \eqref{eq:physical-recovery-reorganized}
and \eqref{eq:P-profiles-revised} give
\[
 \|u_{\neq}(1+s)\|_{L^2}\leq C\varepsilon\mathrm e^{-2\gamma\nu^{1/3}s}.
\]
Moreover, velocity reconstruction
\eqref{eq:velocity-reconstruction-final} and the streamwise spectral
gap imply
\[
 \|u_{\neq}(1+s)\|_{L^2}\leq C\Pi_0(s),\qquad
 \|\nabla u_{\neq}(1+s)\|_{L^2}\leq C(\Pi_0(s)+\Pi_1(s)).
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:P-profiles-revised} gives the two time-integrated
bounds in \eqref{eq:global-ED-spacetime} on $[1,\infty)$.
Here the contribution of $\Pi_0$ to the gradient bound costs
$\nu^{1/2}\nu^{-1/6}=\nu^{1/3}\leq1$.
Taking $\lambda_*=\gamma$, the change from $s$ to $t$ costs at most
$\mathrm e^{\lambda_*}$. The short-time $H^2$ estimate
\eqref{eq:H2-restart-smoothing-global} then proves
\eqref{eq:full-ED-final}--\eqref{eq:global-ED-spacetime} on the full
physical half-line.

The inviscid-damping component of $X_{2\gamma}$, applied to
$\Delta u^2_{\neq}$ in $E_4$, is particularly simple:
\[
 \nabla\Delta^{-1}\partial_x\Delta u^2_{\neq}
 =\partial_x\nabla u^2_{\neq}.
\]
The nonzero streamwise frequency also gives
$\|u^2_{\neq}\|_{H^1}\leq C\|\partial_x\nabla u^2_{\neq}\|_{L^2}$.
Therefore
\[
 \|\mathrm e^{2\gamma\nu^{1/3}s}u^2_{\neq}(1+s)\|_{L_s^2H^1}
 +\|\mathrm e^{2\gamma\nu^{1/3}s}
 \partial_x\nabla u^2_{\neq}(1+s)\|_{L_s^2L^2}
 \leq CE_4(\infty)\leq C\varepsilon.
\]
The same time translation and short-time $H^2$ bound prove
\eqref{eq:global-inviscid-damping}.

For the roll, all unweighted $Y^m$ components on $t\geq1$ are invariant under the time translation, and \eqref{eq:restart-mu-comparison} converts the restarted $\mu_\nu^{1/2}$ component to the physical weight with only an absolute loss. On $0\leq t\leq1$, the $L_t^\infty H^2$ and $\nu^{1/2}L_t^2H^3$ bounds in \eqref{eq:H2-restart-smoothing-global} control
		\begin{equation*}
			\|\Delta_\perp u^2_{0}\|_{Y^0(0,1)}
			+\|u^3_{0}\|_{Y^1(0,1)}
			+\|\mu_\nu^{1/2}\Delta_\perp u^3_{0}\|_{Y^0(0,1)}
			+\nu^{1/2}\|u^\perp_{0}\|_{L^2(0,1;L^2)}
			\leq C\varepsilon.
		\end{equation*}
		Together with the short-time Besov bound \eqref{eq:H2-restart-besov-global} and the restarted $E_{2}$ estimate, this proves \eqref{eq:full-roll-final}, and in particular
\eqref{eq:global-roll-endpoint}, on the full physical half-line.
		
		For the pointwise roll decay, set
$F(s):=(u^\perp_{\neq}\otimes u^\perp_{\neq})_{0}(1+s)$.
The wave-stress estimate \eqref{eq:wave-roll-forcing-revised} and
$E_4(\infty)\leq C\varepsilon$ imply
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^\infty(1+\nu s)^3\|F(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
 \leq C\|\mathrm e^{4\gamma\nu^{1/3}s}F\|_{L_s^2L^2}^2
 \leq C\nu^{-1}\varepsilon^4.
 \label{eq:cubic-weight-wave-stress}
\end{equation}
The first inequality follows from
$\sup_{s\geq0}(1+\nu s)^3\mathrm e^{-8\gamma\nu^{1/3}s}\leq C_\gamma$,
since $0<\nu\leq1$. Apply \eqref{eq:E-decay} to the restarted roll.
Its initial $L^2$ norm and propagated Besov norm are bounded by
$C\varepsilon$, so \eqref{eq:cubic-weight-wave-stress} yields
\begin{align*}
 \|u^\perp_{0}(1+s)\|_{L^2}^2
 &\leq \frac{C\varepsilon^2}{(1+\nu s)^2}
 +\frac{C\varepsilon^4}{\nu^2(1+\nu s)^3}
 \leq\frac{C\varepsilon^2}{(1+\nu s)^2}.
\end{align*}
In the last step, $\varepsilon/\nu\leq c_*$ was used.
Since $1+\nu(t-1)\geq(1+\nu t)/2$ for $t\geq1$, this gives
\eqref{eq:global-roll-decay} on $[1,\infty)$. The short-time
$H^2$ estimate supplies the remaining interval.

Finally, time translation leaves the unweighted $H^4$, dissipative,
and $\partial_tu^1_{0}$ components of $E_1$ unchanged. Its global
bound in \eqref{eq:full-energy-final} proves
\eqref{eq:full-zero-final}.

$\dot H^{-2}=\dot B^{-2}_{2,2}\hookrightarrow\dot B^{-2}_{2,\infty}$

title: Proof
body_md:
The initial roll belongs to $L^1(\mathbb R^2)$: its integral on the unit
ball is controlled by its $L^2$ norm, and its integral outside the
ball is controlled by the first moment. Since it is divergence free,
\Cref{prop:moment} gives
\[
 \|u^\perp_{0,\rm in}\|_{\dot B^{-2}_{2,\infty}}
 \leq C\||x_\perp|u^\perp_{0,\rm in}\|_{L^1}.
\]
Thus $\varepsilon\leq C\varepsilon_m$, and $Cc_m\leq c_*$ ensures
that both main theorems apply. For $\sigma>2$, Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \||x_\perp|u^\perp_{0,\rm in}\|_{L^1}
 \leq\bigl\||x_\perp|\langle x_\perp\rangle^{-\sigma}\bigr\|_{L^2}
 \|\langle x_\perp\rangle^\sigma u^\perp_{0,\rm in}\|_{L^2}
 \leq C_\sigma\varepsilon_\sigma.
\]
Choosing $c_\sigma$ accordingly proves the last assertion.

\eqref{eq:bad-wave3-weighted-revised}; the additional factor

\label{prop:complementary-transverse-closure}
		There exist absolute constants $\delta_3,\gamma_3>0$ and $C>0$ such that the following holds. Assume \eqref{eq:variable-small-assumption} with $\delta_{0}$ replaced by $\delta_3$, and let $(w^2,w^3,p)$ solve \eqref{eq:transverse-forced-system}--\eqref{eq:transverse-forced-pressure}. Then, for $0\leq\sigma\leq\gamma_3$,
		\begin{align}
			&\mathcal E_{\perp,\sigma}(T)
			+\nu^{4/3}\|\Delta w^3\|_{X_\sigma}^2
			\nonumber\\
			&\quad\leq C\Big(
			\|(w^2,w^3)(0)\|_{H^2}^2
			+\|\Delta q(0)\|_{L^2}^2
			\nonumber\\
			&\qquad\qquad
			+\nu^{-1}\|\mathrm e^{\sigma\nu^{1/3}t}\nabla (g^2+\kappa g^3)\|_{L_t^2L_x^2}^2
			+\nu^{-1}\|\mathrm e^{\sigma\nu^{1/3}t}\partial_x g^3\|_{L_t^2L_x^2}^2
			\nonumber\\
			&\qquad\qquad
			+\nu^{-1/3}\|\mathrm e^{\sigma\nu^{1/3}t}\nabla g^3\|_{L_t^2L_x^2}^2
			\Big).
			\label{eq:complementary-transverse-final}
		\end{align}
		No spanwise spectral gap is used; the corresponding modal constants are uniform in $\ell\in\mathbb R$ and remain uniform after integration over the continuous $z$-Fourier variable.

label: eq:lambda-summability
title: Proof
body_md:
For $j=x$, the bilinear arguments identified above use Fourier series
only in $x$ and
two-dimensional Sobolev inequalities on the transverse section.
They therefore apply with that section replaced by $\mathbb R^2$.
For $j=z$, one cannot interchange $x$ and $z$ as in the periodic
proof. Instead use the Fourier transform in $z$ and the same
convolution argument, since
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{k\in2\pi\mathbb Z}(1+k^2)^{-1}<\infty,
 \qquad \int_{\mathbb R}(1+\ell^2)^{-1}\,d\ell<\infty.
 \label{eq:lambda-summability}
\end{equation}
On the remaining section $M=\mathbb T_x\times\mathbb R_y$,
the inhomogeneous Agmon inequality gives
\begin{equation*}
 |\ell|^2\|g_\ell\|_{L^\infty(M)}^2
 \leq C\bigl(\ell^4\|g_\ell\|_{L^2}^2
       +\|\Delta_Mg_\ell\|_{L^2}^2+\|g_\ell\|_{L^2}^2\bigr).
\end{equation*}
The last term is controlled by $\|\Delta g\|_{L^2}^2$ after integration
because $g_{0}=0$. This verifies the Laplacian bound in
\eqref{eq:bilinear-good-derivative}, including small $\ell$.
For the two-level estimates, use instead
$\|h\|_{L^4(M)}^2\leq C\|h\|_{L^2}\|h\|_{H^1(M)}$.
The remaining Minkowski, Cauchy--Schwarz, and Leibniz steps are
unchanged, with integrals replacing sums.

body_md:
In the high-order product estimate identified above, take
$k=m$ and $(f_1,f_2)=(f,g)$.
The proof uses the two-level product estimate with distinguished
direction $x$, the condition $f_{0}=0$, Leibniz expansion, and
Sobolev interpolation. The product estimate on the present domain
is \eqref{eq:bilinear-two-level}; the other steps are unchanged.
In particular, the only Poincar\'e inequality is in $x$.

label: lem:Besov-lower-semicontinuity-final
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For fixed $j,t$, strong $L^2$ convergence gives
$2^{-2j}\|\dot\Delta_jf(t)\|_{L^2}
=\lim_n2^{-2j}\|\dot\Delta_jf_n(t)\|_{L^2}$.
The latter is bounded by the lower limit of
$\sup_{s\leq T}\|f_n(s)\|_{\dot B^{-2}_{2,\infty}}$.
Take the supremum over $j,t$ to obtain \eqref{eq:Besov-lsc-terminal}.

label: lem:H4-approx-stability-final
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Interpolation gives $u_n\to u$ in $C_tH^{3+\theta}$ for $0<\theta<1$.
For the zero modes, $H^{3+\theta}(\mathbb R^2)\hookrightarrow W^{2,\infty}$;
the uniform admissibility and Moser estimates therefore give convergence
of the shear maps and their inverses in $C_tW^{2,\infty}$, and
\begin{equation*}
 \kappa_n\to\kappa\quad\hbox{in }C_tH^{2+\theta},\qquad
 (\rho_{1,n},\rho_{2,n})\to(\rho_1,\rho_2)
 \quad\hbox{in }C_tH^{1+\theta}.
\end{equation*}
Apply the difference energy estimate to \eqref{eq:corrector-Kelvin-equations}.
The forcing differences tend to zero in $L_t^2H^1$ for $q^{(2)}$
and in $L_t^2H^2$ for $q^{(3)}$, including the differences of the
transport coefficients. Hence
\begin{equation*}
 \widetilde{q_n^{(2)}}\to\widetilde{q^{(2)}}\quad\hbox{in }C_tH^1\cap L_t^2H^2,
 \qquad
 \widetilde{q_n^{(3)}}\to\widetilde{q^{(3)}}\quad\hbox{in }C_tH^2\cap L_t^2H^3.
\end{equation*}
Uniform top-order energy bounds and uniqueness identify the weak limits
with the correctors of $u$. The defining formulas then give the corresponding
convergence of $q^{(1)}$, $\Delta u^3_{\neq}-2\partial_xq^{(3)}$,
and the elliptic auxiliary fields. The streak equation similarly identifies
the weak-star limit of $\partial_tu^1_{0,n}$ in $L_t^\infty H^2$.
Weak lower semicontinuity proves the Sobolev energy bounds, and
\Cref{lem:Besov-lower-semicontinuity-final} gives
\eqref{eq:H4-approx-Besov-lsc} from the strong $C_tL^2$ convergence of the rolls.
